title: Learning To Erase Quantum States: Thermodynamic Implications Of Quantum Learning Theory
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental thermodynamic costs for learning and erasing quantum states, connecting quantum learning theory to information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the energy requirements of quantum information processing, specifically the thermodynamic cost of erasing quantum states in the context of quantum learning.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the work required to erase a quantum state based on its complexity, using concepts from quantum learning theory and statistical mechanics.
result: They find that erasing a quantum state that is hard to learn requires more work, establishing a trade-off between learnability and thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results have implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum computers and for understanding the physical limits of quantum learning algorithms.

title: Single- And Two-mode Magnon Thermal Squeezing
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermal squeezing of magnons in a ferrimagnetic insulator, achieving noise below thermal levels.
motivation: To realize squeezed states in magnets for spin-based sensing and information technology.
method: Experimental setup using a ferrimagnetic insulator device to generate and measure thermal magnon squeezing.
result: Demonstrated thermal squeezing of magnons, where noise drops below thermal levels.
conclusion: Opens new possibilities for quantum sensing and information processing using magnon squeezed states.

title: Lieb–Liniger Interaction Via Self-interacting Stationary Light Polaritons
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates a method to realize Lieb-Liniger interactions using self-interacting stationary light polaritons in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To engineer strong effective interactions between photons for quantum simulation of many-body physics, specifically the Lieb-Liniger model.
method: The authors use electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in a cold atomic ensemble to create stationary light polaritons, and then introduce a Kerr nonlinearity via a control field to induce self-interactions.
result: They show that the stationary light polaritons acquire a contact interaction, mapping the system to the Lieb-Liniger model, and analyze the resulting quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying integrable many-body systems with photons and could be extended to more complex quantum simulations.

title: Quantum Metrology Based On Superconducting Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper explores quantum metrology using superconducting qubits, likely leveraging their coherence and control for precision measurements.
motivation: To advance quantum metrology by exploiting the unique properties of superconducting qubits, which are a leading platform for quantum information processing.
method: The paper likely employs theoretical analysis or experimental demonstrations of metrological protocols using superconducting qubit systems, possibly including error mitigation or entanglement-enhanced sensing.
result: Key findings probably include improved measurement precision beyond classical limits, demonstrating the utility of superconducting qubits for quantum metrology.
conclusion: The work establishes superconducting qubits as a viable platform for quantum metrology, with implications for sensing and fundamental tests, and suggests future integration with other quantum systems.

title: Experimental Realization Of Qubit-state-controlled Directional Edge States In Waveguide Qed
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates qubit-state-controlled directional edge states in a waveguide QED system, realizing a topological quantum optical switch.
motivation: To explore the interplay between topology and quantum nonlinearity in waveguide QED, enabling control of edge state propagation via qubit state for potential quantum information processing.
method: The experiment uses a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a photonic waveguide with engineered couplings to realize a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, and measures the directional transmission of microwave photons conditioned on the qubit state.
result: They observe that the qubit state (ground or excited) controls the direction of edge state propagation, achieving high contrast directional transport and demonstrating a quantum switch based on topological edge states.
conclusion: This work establishes a new platform for topological quantum optics with active control, paving the way for quantum routers, switches, and nonreciprocal devices in quantum networks.

title: Fully Passive Received Quantum Access Network Based On Reference-frame-independent Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a fully passive received quantum access network using reference-frame-independent QKD, eliminating active components at the user side.
motivation: To reduce cost and complexity of quantum access networks by removing active optical components (e.g., lasers) from user terminals, making QKD more practical for widespread deployment.
method: The authors design a network architecture where users only have passive receivers, and the central office generates and distributes quantum signals. They employ reference-frame-independent QKD to avoid active alignment of reference frames.
result: The proposed scheme achieves secure key rates comparable to active systems while significantly simplifying user hardware. Experimental or simulation results demonstrate feasibility over typical access network distances.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum communication by enabling passive user terminals, potentially lowering barriers for quantum network adoption. Future work may focus on integration with existing fiber infrastructure and scaling to more users.

title: Scalable All-solid-state Cavity Qed On A Hybrid Quantum Dot–lithium Niobate Platform
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a scalable all-solid-state cavity QED platform using a quantum dot coupled to a lithium niobate photonic crystal cavity, achieving strong coupling and high cooperativity.
motivation: To realize scalable, integrated cavity QED systems for quantum information processing, overcoming limitations of traditional approaches like atomic systems or fragile cryogenic setups.
method: Fabrication of a hybrid device combining InAs/GaAs quantum dots with a lithium niobate photonic crystal cavity, using nanofabrication techniques and optical characterization at cryogenic temperatures.
result: Demonstration of strong coupling between a single quantum dot and the cavity mode, with a cooperativity exceeding 10, and evidence of vacuum Rabi splitting.
conclusion: The hybrid platform offers a promising route toward scalable quantum networks and on-chip quantum optics, with potential for integration with other quantum systems.

title: Identifying Quantum Resources In Encoded Computations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper develops a framework to identify and quantify quantum resources (entanglement, coherence) in encoded computations, linking resource theory to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: To understand which quantum resources are essential for quantum advantage in encoded (fault-tolerant) computations, and to provide a resource-theoretic perspective on quantum error correction.
method: The authors use resource theories (e.g., entanglement, coherence) and apply them to encoded logical states, analyzing how resources transform under encoding and error correction operations.
result: They show that certain resources like magic states and entanglement are necessary for universal encoded computation, and provide measures to quantify them in logical qubits.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum resource theories and fault-tolerant quantum computing, offering insights for designing resource-efficient quantum algorithms and error-correcting codes.

title: Hong–Ou–Mandel Interference Of More Than Ten Indistinguishable Atoms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstration of Hong–Ou–Mandel interference with up to 12 indistinguishable atoms, showing multiparticle interference patterns with single-atom resolution.
motivation: Extending HOM interference to many massive particles is challenging; this work aims to observe genuine multiparticle interference in atomic ensembles.
method: Trapped ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, with single-atom detection and negligible loss, measuring interference patterns as a function of atom number.
result: Clear multiparticle interference patterns observed for up to 12 atoms, with high indistinguishability and low loss.
conclusion: Opens new possibilities for quantum metrology and tests of quantum mechanics with massive particles; future work may scale to larger ensembles.

title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Most studies of collective light scattering in atomic arrays have focused on 1D and 2D systems; this work extends to 3D arrays to explore new phenomena.
method: Experimental realization of a 3D atomic array and measurement of coherent light scattering suppression.
result: Strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering was observed in the 3D array.
conclusion: The findings open new possibilities for controlling light-matter interactions in 3D atomic arrays, with potential applications in quantum optics and information.

title: Quantum Coherent Beating In Polar Disubphthalocyanine-fullerene Cocrystals For Ultrafast Photothermal Conversion
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports quantum coherent beating and ultrafast photothermal conversion in a polar disubphthalocyanine-fullerene cocrystal, achieving high temperatures under low laser intensity.
motivation: To explore organic cocrystals for efficient photothermal conversion, leveraging quantum coherent effects for ultrafast energy transfer.
method: Synthesis of polar disubphthalocyanine-fullerene cocrystals, followed by optical spectroscopy and photothermal measurements.
result: Observed quantum coherent beating and ultrafast energy transfer; temperature reached 228°C in 5 s under 0.5 W cm−2 laser, with equilibrium at 242°C.
conclusion: Demonstrates potential of organic cocrystals for photothermal applications, but relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is limited.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: This review surveys chaotic photonics in microresonators, focusing on harnessing chaotic dynamics for technology and science.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of chaotic microcavity photonics across materials and architectures, highlighting opportunities for innovation.
method: Review of existing literature and experimental/theoretical advances in chaotic microresonators.
result: Chaotic dynamics in microresonators can be harnessed for various applications, though specific findings are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: Chaotic photonics offers a source of innovation; further exploration of materials and architectures is encouraged.

title: Cross-probing Van Der Waals Multiferroics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: This review advocates for cross-probing techniques to identify intrinsic multiferroicity in van der Waals multiferroics.
motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional probing methods in detecting intrinsic multiferroicity in atomically thin materials.
method: Review of cross-probing technologies combining magnetic and electric probes.
result: Cross-probing can distinguish intrinsic multiferroicity from extrinsic effects.
conclusion: Cross-probing is essential for advancing low-power magnetoelectric devices based on van der Waals multiferroics.

title: Vortices And Solitons In Polariton Superfluids And Condensates
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 14 May 2026;
tldr: This review discusses the formation and control of vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates for information processing applications.
motivation: Polariton condensates exhibit nonlinear phenomena like vortices and solitons that could be used for information processing, but a comprehensive review of their formation and control was needed.
method: The authors review experimental and theoretical work on polariton vortices and solitons, covering their generation, stability, and manipulation in microcavity polariton systems.
result: Key findings include the demonstration of quantized phase jumps in vortices and stable soliton shapes, with potential for encoding information.
conclusion: Polariton vortices and solitons offer a platform for nonlinear information processing, but further work is needed to realize practical devices.

title: Scalable Boltzmann Generators For Equilibrium Sampling Of Large-scale Materials
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a scalable Boltzmann Generator for efficient equilibrium sampling of large-scale materials, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: To overcome the computational cost of traditional molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods for equilibrium sampling of materials with over 1,000 atoms.
method: A size-transferable Boltzmann Generator architecture based on normalizing flows, trained on small systems and applied to larger systems.
result: The method enables rapid one-shot equilibrium sampling and accurate absolute free energy calculations for large-scale materials.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable solution for materials simulation, with potential applications in computational materials science.

title: Controlling Unknown Quantum States Via Data-driven State Representations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper develops a data-driven method to control unknown quantum states using machine learning, without requiring prior knowledge of the system.
motivation: Controlling unknown quantum states is challenging because traditional methods rely on accurate system models. The authors aim to bypass this by using data-driven state representations.
method: They propose a framework that learns a representation of the quantum state from measurement data and then uses that representation to design control pulses, likely via reinforcement learning or neural networks.
result: The method successfully controls unknown quantum states in simulations, achieving high fidelity without prior knowledge of the Hamiltonian or state.
conclusion: This approach could enable quantum control in scenarios where system models are unavailable, but its practical applicability to real noisy quantum devices remains to be tested.

title: High-speed Non-volatile Barium Titanate Field-programmable Photonic Gate Array
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a high-speed, non-volatile photonic gate array using barium titanate ferroelectric phase shifters, achieving sub-100-ns switching and zero-static power consumption.
motivation: To develop a programmable photonic integrated circuit that combines fast switching with non-volatile memory to reduce energy consumption.
method: Barium titanate ferroelectric material is used in photonic phase shifters arranged in a hexagonal waveguide mesh, forming a field-programmable photonic gate array.
result: The device achieves sub-100-ns switching speeds and retains its state without continuous power, enhancing energy efficiency.
conclusion: This work advances programmable photonics for applications in optical computing and communications, but its relevance to the user's interests in quantum information thermodynamics, foundations, or communication is minimal.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and cell density control phase transitions in tissue organization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like adhesion and jamming regulate tissue material state and developmental programs.
method: Combined in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.
conclusion: Phase transitions direct developmental programs, highlighting the role of adhesion in tissue organization.

title: Orbital Angular Momentum Multiplexing Diffractive Neural Networks For High-capacity Optical Inference
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents an orbital angular momentum multiplexing diffractive neural network for high-capacity optical inference, achieving 14-fold higher mode utilization and multitask recognition of 100 object categories.
motivation: To overcome the limited mode utilization in conventional orbital angular momentum multiplexing systems and enable high-capacity optical computing for multitask inference.
method: An end-to-end auto-optimization strategy is developed to design diffractive neural networks that exploit orbital angular momentum modes for multiplexing, replacing manual encoding.
result: The approach achieves 14-fold higher mode utilization compared to manual encoding and demonstrates multitask recognition of 100 object categories with an average accuracy of 72.7%.
conclusion: The work advances optical neural networks by leveraging orbital angular momentum multiplexing, potentially enabling high-capacity, low-power optical inference systems.

title: Crystalline Symmetry Breaking Enables Directional Light Emission In Quantum Dots
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports that crystalline symmetry breaking in quantum dots enhances light out-coupling efficiency, achieving high external quantum efficiencies in green QD-LEDs.
motivation: To improve the light extraction efficiency of quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs), which is limited by total internal reflection and waveguide modes.
method: The authors introduce crystalline symmetry breaking in zinc-blende quantum dots to modify the emission pattern and enhance out-coupling, and fabricate green CdZnSe- and InP-based QD-LEDs.
result: External quantum efficiencies of 34.3% for CdZnSe and 31.0% for InP-based QD-LEDs were achieved.
conclusion: This approach offers a new route to high-efficiency QD-LEDs without complex photonic structures, with potential for display and lighting applications.

title: An On-chip Programmable Valley Optoelectronic Nanocircuit
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 25 May 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip programmable valley optoelectronic nanocircuit using meta-waveguide photodetectors integrated with transition metal dichalcogenides for generating, routing, and reading valley-dependent chiral photons.
motivation: To achieve on-chip manipulation of valley-dependent photons for valleytronic applications, enabling programmable optoelectronic nanocircuits.
method: Integration of meta-waveguide photodetectors with transition metal dichalcogenides to create a light-programmable valley optoelectronic nanocircuit.
result: In situ generation, selective routing, and electrical readout of valley-dependent chiral photons were demonstrated.
conclusion: This work advances valleytronics by providing a programmable platform for on-chip valley optoelectronic circuits, with potential applications in quantum information processing and nanophotonics.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the evolution of atomic force microscopy from a surface imaging tool to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the key innovations over 40 years that transformed AFM into a multipurpose measurement platform.
method: Commentary and historical review of technological advancements in AFM.
result: AFM has evolved beyond imaging to enable nanomechanical, electrical, and chemical measurements at the nanoscale.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its capabilities, promising further integration with other techniques for holistic exploration of nanoscale phenomena.

title: Do The Benefits Of Fundamental Physics Research Outweigh Its Wider Societal Costs?
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the societal costs and benefits of fundamental physics research, using economic tools to evaluate sustainability of big science projects.
motivation: To address the complex multi-dimensional problem of whether large-scale fundamental physics projects are sustainable and beneficial to society.
method: The paper applies economic analysis tools to assess the costs and benefits of big science projects.
result: It provides a framework for evaluating sustainability and societal impact of fundamental physics research.
conclusion: Economic tools can help decision-making for big science projects, but the paper does not present specific findings or data.

title: Transparent Conducting Electrodes For Perovskite–silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: This review discusses transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells, focusing on optical, electrical, and interfacial losses and strategies for scalable, low-indium electrodes.
motivation: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells.
method: The paper is a review that examines how optical, electrical and interfacial losses arise in tandem cells and outlines strategies to enable scalable, low-indium electrodes.
result: The review identifies key loss mechanisms and proposes strategies for next-generation electrodes.
conclusion: The paper provides guidance for developing scalable, low-indium transparent conducting electrodes for tandem solar cells.

title: Discovering Expert-level Nash Equilibrium Algorithms With Large Language Models
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses large language models to discover algorithms for computing approximate Nash equilibria, a topic in algorithmic game theory.
motivation: To automate the discovery of equilibrium algorithms with provable worst-case guarantees, surpassing existing multi-player design paradigms.
method: The authors developed LegoNE, a framework that combines symbolic proof encoding with LLMs to automatically certify worst-case guarantees of discovered algorithms.
result: LegoNE discovered new equilibrium algorithms that outperform previous approaches in multi-player settings.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of LLMs for algorithm discovery in game theory, but its relevance to quantum information and thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies adhesion-driven rigidity transitions in embryonic tissues, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like rigidity influence epithelial organization during morphogenesis.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of cell adhesion and density in embryonic tissues.
result: Adhesion-driven rigidification is identified as key to epithelial organization, decoupled from density-driven jamming.
conclusion: Provides insights into tissue mechanics but has no direct connection to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper resolves a decade-long discrepancy in the lifetime of a nuclear metastable state in thorium-229 ions, revealing an uncommon decay channel.
motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, puzzling physicists for about ten years.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis were used to determine the lifetime and identify the decay channel.
result: The solution provides a hint towards an uncommon decay channel, explaining the observed shorter lifetime.
conclusion: The findings resolve the lifetime puzzle and may impact nuclear clock development and fundamental physics studies.

title: Single-shot Full-field X-ray Imaging With 10-nm Resolution Using Hard X-ray Free-electron Laser Pulses
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates single-shot full-field X-ray imaging with 10-nm resolution using hard X-ray free-electron laser pulses and advanced mirror optics.
motivation: To achieve high-resolution imaging of ultrafast phenomena at the nanoscale, overcoming limitations of conventional X-ray imaging techniques.
method: Combined sub-10-nm focusing mirror optics with an algorithm to compensate for illumination fluctuations in a single-shot in-line holography setup using hard X-ray free-electron laser pulses.
result: Achieved a field of view exceeding 1 μm and a spatial resolution of 10 nm in single-shot femtosecond imaging.
conclusion: This technique enables nanoscale imaging of ultrafast dynamics, with potential applications in materials science and biology.

title: Ternary Self-assembled Molecular Contact For Ambient-processed Perovskite/silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a ternary self-assembled molecular contact for ambient-processed perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, achieving 31.72% efficiency.
motivation: To enable high-efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells fabricated under ambient conditions, addressing stability and scalability issues.
method: Development of a ternary self-assembled molecular contact layer and ambient processing techniques for perovskite solar cells.
result: Achieved a power conversion efficiency of 31.72% for perovskite/silicon tandem devices.
conclusion: The ternary molecular contact enables ambient processing of high-efficiency tandem cells, potentially reducing manufacturing costs and improving scalability.

title: Omnidirectional Ionic Locking Network For Stable Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: This paper presents an omnidirectional ionic locking network to stabilize perovskite solar cells, achieving high efficiency and long operational stability.
motivation: Perovskite solar cells suffer from ion migration and instability under operational conditions, limiting their commercial viability.
method: The authors introduce a bifunctional spacer at perovskite grain boundaries that locks ions in place, preventing migration and degradation.
result: The device achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.01% and retained 90% of its initial efficiency after over 2,000 hours of operation.
conclusion: This approach significantly enhances the stability of perovskite photovoltaics, paving the way for durable, high-efficiency solar cells.

title: Transitions Of The Atlantic Ocean Circulation
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 18 May 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation from a dynamical systems perspective, focusing on climate impacts.
motivation: To unify results from ocean-climate models regarding instabilities of Atlantic Ocean flows that can have large climate impacts.
method: A dynamical systems viewpoint is used to review and synthesize results from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models.
result: The paper identifies key instabilities and multistable behaviors in the Atlantic Ocean circulation.
conclusion: The findings have implications for understanding climate change and predicting future ocean circulation shifts.

title: Programmable Nucleic Acid Sensing In Human Cells Using Circularizable ssDNA
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents SONAR, a method for programmable nucleic acid sensing in human cells using circularizable ssDNA.
motivation: To develop tools that can sense nucleic acid signatures in living cells and link detection to programmable gene-control outputs.
method: Target-dependent ssDNA ligation inside cells to detect nucleic acids and drive gene-control outputs.
result: Demonstrated programmable nucleic acid sensing in human cells.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for cellular sensing and gene regulation, but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Li-In-S Composite Foil With Built-in Electric Fields To Stabilize Li/Li<sub>6</sub>PS<sub>5</sub>Cl Interface For Long-life All-solid-state Batteries
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a Li-In-S composite foil with built-in electric fields to stabilize the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface in all-solid-state batteries, improving cycle life.
motivation: Sulfide electrolyte/Li interfacial instability limits the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries.
method: In and S are doped into Li metal to form a composite foil, creating built-in electric fields that stabilize the interface.
result: The approach enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries with improved interfacial stability.
conclusion: The work provides a strategy for stabilizing Li/sulfide electrolyte interfaces, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, suggesting physical constraints shape cell fate.
motivation: To understand the principles governing cell differentiation, specifically whether molecular details or physical constraints dominate methylation dynamics.
method: Analysis of methylation data from early embryos, fitting to scaling laws.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, independent of molecular specifics.
conclusion: Physical constraints may be key drivers of cell fate, with implications for developmental biology and potential cross-disciplinary insights.

title: Evidence For The Generic Existence Of Two Local Structures In Liquid Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: Simulations suggest the existence of two interconvertible local structures in liquid water, supporting the two-state picture of deeply undercooled water.
motivation: To provide evidence for the long-predicted two-state regime in deeply undercooled water.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations.
result: Two local structures that undergo interconvertible reactions were identified.
conclusion: The findings corroborate the two-state picture of water, with implications for understanding water's anomalous properties.

title: Exploring Decolonizing The Curriculum Using Six Thinking Hats
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses decolonizing the physics curriculum using the Six Thinking Hats framework, focusing on pedagogical strategies rather than technical physics research.
motivation: To address competence anxiety among educators when discussing decolonization in physics education.
method: Application of the Six Thinking Hats framework to structure conversations about decolonizing the curriculum.
result: The framework provides a safe and structured way to navigate challenging discussions.
conclusion: The approach may help educators overcome barriers to decolonizing physics education.

title: Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Transmission From Tuberculosis Patients With And Without Recognized Symptoms: A Case-contact Study In Eastern China
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies tuberculosis transmission from symptomatic and asymptomatic patients in Eastern China, finding similar infection risks.
motivation: To understand the role of asymptomatic tuberculosis patients in transmission, which is poorly understood.
method: Case-contact study comparing infection rates among contacts of symptomatic and asymptomatic tuberculosis patients.
result: Both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients pose similar risk of infection to their contacts.
conclusion: Public health strategies should address transmission from minimally symptomatic individuals.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Ba.2.86 And Jn.1 Expand Tropism In Human Proximal Intestinal Epithelium
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the tropism and replication of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants in human intestinal epithelium, with no connection to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.
motivation: To understand the expanded tissue tropism and entry mechanisms of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
method: Infection experiments in human airway and intestinal organoids, analyzing replication efficiency and entry pathways.
result: BA.2.86 and JN.1 replicate efficiently in intestinal enteroids, with JN.1 showing increased gut tropism and low inflammation.
conclusion: These variants may have altered pathogenesis and transmission routes, warranting further surveillance.

title: Vicennial Metagenomic Time Series Unveils Evolutionary Dynamics Of Giant Viruses In A Freshwater Ecosystem
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the evolutionary dynamics of giant viruses in a freshwater lake over 20 years using metagenomics.
motivation: Giant viruses are poorly understood in freshwater ecosystems; the study aims to uncover their genomic adaptation to environmental changes.
method: Metagenomic time-series analysis of 20 years of samples from Lake Mendota, including genome assembly, gene annotation, and phylogenetic analysis.
result: Giant virus genomes show genomic stability but adapt via gene duplication and horizontal gene transfer, with increased virus-host interactions over time.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of giant viruses in freshwater ecosystems and their evolutionary strategies in response to environmental change.

title: Integrative Proteomics And Lipidomics Reveals Dual Roles For Lipid Droplets In The Host Cell Antiviral Response
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses proteomics and lipidomics to study lipid droplets in antiviral response, with no connection to quantum information or physics.
motivation: To understand the role of lipid droplets in host cell antiviral defense.
method: Integrative proteomics and lipidomics analyses of virus-infected cells.
result: Virus-induced lipid droplets recruit antiviral proteins and remodel lipids, forming signaling hubs; long chain fatty acids enhance interferon responses.
conclusion: Lipid droplets have dual roles in antiviral response, suggesting potential therapeutic targets.
